note:
F-9, the account -> firm-plan mapping. This ticket is the CODE half: the reporter must resolve the firm profile per account, the way the ENFORCER has since P1-42. The config half (populating AccountFirmMap on the live box) is an operator action and is not part of this patch.

The acceptance tests were written BY HAND FIRST and are RED at the 1188/7 baseline. tests/*Tests.cs is a PROTECTED path -- you cannot reach it and must not try. Seven assertions fail now and must pass; the other 1188 must STAY passing, and three of those existing ones constrain this fix tightly. Read the spec's item 5.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. `EvaluateFirmMirror` calls `ResolveEffectiveFirmConfig(fm, accountName)` and enforces the resolved plan's numbers -- it flattens the position and locks the account out. `GuardRuleRegistry`'s two firm rules never followed: they branch on the TOP-LEVEL sub-rule switch and report the TOP-LEVEL Amount. The hand-written matrix test found FOUR disagreements, in BOTH directions, on the exact shapes the researched firm profiles use:
  reporter=Disabled  enforcer=FIRES   (top-level off, plan's rule on)   -> the UI hides live protection
  reporter=Enforcing enforcer=silent  (top-level on, plan's rule off)   -> the UI claims protection that cannot fire
The second is the shape of the real Take Profit Trader profile, whose DailyLoss is deliberately OFF because TPT has no daily loss limit.

This was latent only because `AccountFirmMap` is EMPTY on this box. F-9 populates it, so F-9 activates it.

tickets.title: F-9: the firm-rule REPORTER reads the top-level block while the ENFORCER enforces the account's resolved firm plan
tickets.defect:
`GuardRules.cs` declares two firm rules whose evaluators read `c.Config.FirmMirror.TrailingDD` / `.DailyLoss` -- the TOP-LEVEL block. Since `P1-42` the enforcer does not: `EvaluateFirmMirror` calls `RiskGuardAddOn.ResolveEffectiveFirmConfig(fm, accountName)` first and substitutes the mapped firm profile's `TrailingDD`/`DailyLoss`. The two paths therefore disagree whenever an account is mapped to a profile whose sub-rule switch differs from the top-level one, which is EVERY shape the four researched profiles use.

Concretely, both directions are live:

(a) Top-level `TrailingDD.Enabled = false` with a mapped plan whose `TrailingDD.Enabled = true` -- the observed live/researched shape. The evaluator short-circuits and reports `Disabled - firm trailing drawdown not enabled`, while the guard flattens the position and locks the account out on that plan's numbers. The inventory hides live protection, and an operator reading it would go and switch the top-level block on, which applies the guessed 2500 to every unmapped account.

(b) Top-level `DailyLoss.Enabled = true` with a mapped plan whose `DailyLoss.Enabled = false` -- the real Take Profit Trader profile, which has no daily loss limit at all. The evaluator reports the rule as `Enforcing` against the top-level 1500 while nothing can ever fire. This is the reassuring direction, and it is the one that costs money.

Separately, the EVIDENCE COUNT is `AccountFirmMap.Count` -- a GLOBAL count on a rule declared `Scope = PerAccount` with `EvidenceLabel = "accounts mapped to a firm"`. One mapped account therefore reports evidence for all 96 accounts the live box lists, 88 of which are expired prop accounts. And the reported `Limit` is the top-level `Amount`, so a mapped account is shown a number it is not being held to.
tickets.spec:
In `addons/GuardRules.cs`, rewrite the two firm rule evaluators so that each resolves the effective config for `c.AccountName` and reports THAT. Both regions get the same shape; only the sub-rule, the current value and the limit's sign differ.

1. RESOLVE ONCE, per account. `RiskGuardAddOn.ResolveEffectiveFirmConfig(fm, c.AccountName)` is `internal static` in the same assembly -- call it, do not reimplement the lookup. It already handles null dictionaries, an unmapped account, a mapping to an absent firm, and a profile that omits a sub-rule, and it is OrdinalIgnoreCase on both dictionaries. Reimplementing any part of that is how the two paths diverge again.

2. THE MASTER SWITCH FIRST. If `fm` is null or `!fm.Enabled`, return `Off(...)`. `FirmMirror.Enabled` is checked by the enforcer's CALLERS (RiskGuardAddOn.cs:1431 and :1502), not by `ComputeFirmMirror`, so it must be honoured here too or the reporter claims a rule the guard never reaches.

3. THEN THE RESOLVED SUB-RULE. Take the sub-rule off the RESOLVED config, not off `fm`. If it is null or `!Enabled`, return `Off(...)`.

4. OTHERWISE `R(current, limit, evidence, note)` where:
   - `limit` is the RESOLVED sub-rule's `Amount` -- `eff.TrailingDD.Amount` for the trailing rule, and `-Math.Abs(eff.DailyLoss.Amount)` for the daily-loss rule, whose existing negative sign convention must be preserved.
   - `current` is unchanged from today: `c.Account == null ? (double?)null : c.Account.AccountEquity` for the trailing rule, and `...RealizedPnL` for the daily-loss rule.
   - `evidence` is 1 when THIS account has a non-empty entry in `fm.AccountFirmMap`, else 0. NOT `AccountFirmMap.Count`. Note carefully: the test is whether the account has a MAPPING, not whether that mapping RESOLVES to a present profile -- see item 5.
   - `note` names what the operator has to check. Three cases, and each must be distinguishable in the text: unmapped (say that the numbers in force are the top-level block and that it was chosen for no stated account size); mapped and resolved (name the plan key); mapped to a firm ABSENT from `FirmProfiles` (name the firm key, and say that preflight refuses to arm on it and that the top-level fallback is what is in force).

5. THREE EXISTING TESTS CONSTRAIN THIS, and two of them will fail if you get the evidence rule wrong in the obvious ways:
   - An account with NO mapping must report `Inert` even though the top-level block would fire for it. That is a deliberate decision already pinned by `TestUi3_AnEmptyCollectionCanNeverReportEnforcing`: a firm rule evaluating the guessed top-level number is not firm protection, and must never render green. Do NOT 'fix' this by counting the fallback as evidence.
   - A rule with an `EvidenceLabel` must have an evidence count that MOVES when its collection is populated. A test derives that rather than trusting the label. If you count evidence as 'resolves to a present profile', the count stays 0 for the mapped-but-dangling case that test uses, the count stops varying, and it fails. This is why item 4 says mapping, not resolution.
   - `Off()` deliberately sets `EvidenceCount = 1` so a switched-off rule reports `Disabled` rather than `Inert`. Do not change `Off`, `R`, or `DeriveState`.

6. Change NOTHING outside the two rule definitions. Do not add a field to `GuardRuleReading` or `GuardRuleRow`, do not touch the `GuardNonRule` list, do not touch any other rule, and do not alter `ResolveEffectiveFirmConfig` itself -- the enforcer depends on it and its behaviour is already pinned by `TestP1_42_MappedAccountIsEvaluatedAgainstItsFirmProfile`.

7. A block-bodied lambda is expected here and is fine; the surrounding rules use expression lambdas only because they fit on one. Keep the existing 4-space indentation and the `new GuardRuleDefinition { ... }` shape.
tickets.context:
`GuardRules.cs` is the guard-side rule inventory -- see its file header and docs/UI_REDESIGN_DESIGN.md section 6a. It is host-agnostic: it takes config and snapshots and reaches for no engine, which is what lets the suite build these situations without an NT8 in the room.

The vocabulary, from `GuardRuleState`, worst first: `ConfiguredNotEvaluated` (in the file, no code evaluates it), `Inert` (evaluated, evidence set EMPTY, verdict a foregone conclusion), `EvaluatedNotEnforcing`, `Enforcing`, `Disabled` (switched off by the operator -- not a defect). `DeriveState` is the ONLY place that vocabulary lives: `DisabledByConfig` wins, then `EvidenceCount <= 0` gives `Inert`, then `guardCanAct`.

`R(current, limit, evidence, note)` and `Off(note)` are the two private helpers at the top of the registry. `Off` sets `DisabledByConfig = true` AND `EvidenceCount = 1`.

The resolver you must call, `RiskGuardAddOn.ResolveEffectiveFirmConfig(FirmMirrorConfig fm, string accountName)` at RiskGuardAddOn.cs:4554, returns a NEW `FirmMirrorConfig` whose `TrailingDD`/`DailyLoss` are the mapped profile's, keeping the daily boundary (a property of the clock, not of the firm) and carrying both dictionaries through. It returns `fm` ITSELF -- not a copy -- when there is nothing to resolve: null input, empty account name, either dictionary null, no mapping, an empty firm name, an absent profile, or a null profile. Reference equality is therefore NOT a reliable test for 'did it resolve'; check the dictionaries.

The four researched firm profiles, recovered from a 2026-08-07 config backup on this box, are the shapes this has to be right for:
  TakeProfitTrader  TrailingDD eod 1500/200            DailyLoss OFF
  Tradeify          TrailingDD eod 2000/200 lock 100   DailyLoss include_unrealized_peak 1250/100
  Lucid             TrailingDD eod 2500/200            DailyLoss include_unrealized_peak 2500/200
  Apex              TrailingDD eod 2000/200            DailyLoss include_unrealized_peak 1000/100
Note that two of the four have a sub-rule switched OFF or set differently from the top-level block. That is not an edge case; it is the norm.
expect_green: the reporter never calls a rule Disabled that the enforcer runs
the trailing-drawdown limit reported is the plan's 1500
the note names the firm plan the account resolved to
the daily-loss limit reported is the plan's 1250
a mapping to an absent profile still names the firm it points at
an account absent from a 3-entry map reports Inert with 0 evidence
the mapped account itself still reports Enforcing on 1 piece of evidence

regions.note:
THE WHOLE RULE LIST, and exactly TWO of its entries change: the one whose ConfigPath is "FirmMirror.TrailingDD.Amount" and the one whose ConfigPath is "FirmMirror.DailyLoss.Amount". Every other entry must come back BYTE-IDENTICAL -- 22 other rules and the GuardNonRule list downstream of them are pinned by the UI3 classification gate and by 1188 passing assertions, and this region is large only because a C# collection initializer has no smaller enclosing declaration to anchor on.

Within the two entries that change: keep Name, ConfigPath, EvidenceLabel, Source = GuardRuleSource.FirmProfile and Scope = GuardRuleScope.PerAccount exactly as they are. ConfigPath is the registry key the classification gate matches on and a test asserts no path is declared twice. Only the Evaluator body changes.

The two differ in three ways: CurrentValue is c.Account.AccountEquity for the trailing rule and c.Account.RealizedPnL for the daily-loss rule; the daily-loss limit keeps its existing NEGATIVE sign convention, -Math.Abs(eff.DailyLoss.Amount); and the daily-loss rule has no note today and needs one. The real Take Profit Trader profile has DailyLoss OFF, so the mapped-plan-disabled path is that rule's normal case, not an edge case.
